scene: Wolves have come down from the hills after a hard winter and taken six lambs. Your Ligurian shepherds want to hunt them their way.

choices.label: Hunt with the shepherds
choices.resultText: Three wolves and a boar nobody planned on. The shepherds sing about it, and you are the Greek in the song.

choices.label: Hire a citizen huntsman
choices.resultText: He kills two wolves and charges for three. The shepherds are polite about it, which is worse than anything.

scene: A neighbor upstream has dammed the mill-stream for his own new wheel. Your mill has turned once this week.

choices.label: Take him before the magistrates
choices.resultText: Water rights older than his wheel. The dam comes down. He builds a smaller one, legally, and you both grind slower.

choices.label: Open the dam yourself one dark night
choices.resultText: A pick, a moon, a torrent. Your mill turns all week. He rebuilds. This will go on.

scene: Plowing a new field turns up a stone-lined tomb: a Ligurian warrior, a bronze sword, gold at the throat.

choices.label: Take the gold, replant the field
choices.resultText: The gold sells. The field yields badly for three years. The Ligurian hands will not work it.

choices.label: Rebury him with rites and a wall
choices.resultText: A stone wall around a stone tomb. Ligurian shepherds leave things at it. Your harvests, they say, are why.

scene: The Archons offer you the keys to the public granary for a year: the city's bread in your keeping, and no pay but the name.

choices.label: Take the keys
choices.resultText: A year of counting, weighing, and refusing bribes. When the city hungers, it now knocks at your door.

choices.label: Decline; your own barns are enough
choices.resultText: Another House takes the keys and the name. You keep your evenings.

scene: The marsh at the edge of your land could be cut into salt-pans. The work is brutal and the Ligurians who know how want a share, not wages.

choices.label: Give them the share
choices.resultText: Salt by autumn, and a village of partners at the marsh edge who defend it like their own. It is.

choices.label: Wages only, and Greek overseers
choices.resultText: Salt by winter. Two overseers quit. The pans are yours and nobody else's, which is the point and the problem.

scene: Wild bees have swarmed in your oldest olive. A Ligurian boy says he can take them into hives without smoke.

choices.label: Let him try
choices.resultText: He talks to them. You do not believe it and they go into the hives. Thyme honey by autumn, and the boy is on wages.

choices.label: Smoke them out the Greek way
choices.resultText: Honey, smoke, and a swarm that leaves for the neighbor's grove. He thanks you the next year.

scene: Ligurian shepherds ask to bring their flocks through your lower fields to the summer hills, as their grandfathers did before there were fields.

choices.label: Allow the passage, and ask for the manure
choices.resultText: The flocks pass in a week and leave your fallow rich. The shepherds leave cheese. Old roads, it turns out, pay.

choices.label: Fence the fields and turn them
choices.resultText: They go round, slowly, through a neighbor's land. Something in the neighbor's fence is broken by autumn, and the neighbor looks at you.

scene: A smallholder neighbor asks to use your press for his olives, having none. He can pay in oil, next year, probably.

choices.label: Lend it for a tithe of the oil
choices.resultText: His oil is better than yours, annoyingly. The tithe is worth having and so is the neighbor.

choices.label: Rent it at the going rate, in silver
choices.resultText: He pays, in silver he borrowed. Next year he sells the grove to a Rhodian and moves to Emporion.

scene: The tax assessor walks your groves with a rod and an opinion. He counts trees generously in his favor.

choices.label: Walk with him and count every tree yourself
choices.resultText: Four hundred and six, not four hundred and forty. He is annoyed and correct. The tax is right.

choices.label: Invite him to dinner before he finishes counting
choices.resultText: Three hundred and eighty. Excellent wine. He will be back next year, hungry.

scene: A rot is in the new vines. A Greek vintner says pull them; a Gaulish woman from the hill says sulphur and a prayer to something she will not name.

choices.label: Pull the vines
choices.resultText: Three years lost. The rot does not spread. Hesiod would approve, and Hesiod never planted vines here.

choices.label: Try the Gaulish cure
choices.resultText: Sulphur, smoke, and a bundle at the field's corner you do not ask about. The vines live. The priest of Apollo asks what the bundle was.

scene: Land in Agathe's chora is going cheap: the Volcae are near, and the settlers are nervous.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.resultText: Good soil, a nervous tenant, and a steward who sleeps with a spear. Agathe's magistrates are glad of one more owner with a stake in the wall.

choices.label: Pass; buy nothing you cannot walk to
choices.resultText: A Rhodian buys it. Ten years later he is very rich, or very dead. You hear both stories.

scene: The south field has no water. A diviner with a forked stick will find it for a fee; a Greek engineer will find it for four fees.

choices.label: Pay the diviner
choices.resultText: He walks, the stick dips, you dig, there is water. You will never know whether the stick knew or he did.

choices.label: Pay the engineer
choices.resultText: He draws the field, explains the slope, and finds water where the diviner would have. You understand why, which costs extra.

scene: The first olives of the year. Custom says the first basket goes to Artemis; your steward says the first basket is the best oil.

choices.label: Carry the basket to the temple yourself
choices.resultText: The priestess anoints the altar with your oil. The rest of the pressing sells better for having been blessed by association.

choices.label: Press it, and send the second basket
choices.resultText: The best oil sells to a Kleitos. The temple gets good oil. The priestess can tell the difference, and says so.

scene: A tenant family has slipped away in the night owing two years' rent, leaving the plot and a note in bad Greek apologizing.

choices.label: Let it go and re-let the plot
choices.resultText: A new family, better at farming and worse at writing. The note you keep, for reasons you do not examine.

choices.label: Send men after them to Emporion
choices.resultText: They are found, and pay in a cart and two goats. The cart is worth having. The goats look at you.

scene: The shipyards want the old oaks on your ridge for keels. They are your grandfather's oaks and worth a fortune in a war year.

choices.label: Sell the oaks
choices.resultText: Keels for two pentekonters. The ridge is bare and your grandfather's shade, you feel, is not pleased.

choices.label: Keep them, and sell the yard the young ash instead
choices.resultText: Masts, not keels. The yard grumbles and pays. The oaks stand, and so, in a manner of speaking, does he.

scene: The boundary with your Ligurian neighbor has never been sworn. He proposes an oath by his gods and yours, at the stone, with both households watching.

choices.label: Swear it, both ways
choices.resultText: Wine on the stone, blood on the stone, and a line that neither House's sons will move. It holds for a generation.

choices.label: Swear by Greek law only, with a magistrate
choices.resultText: A document, a seal, a stone. He signs it and does not swear. It holds as long as the magistrate lives.

scene: A prospector finds silver-bearing rock in your hill, or says he does. Mining it needs slaves, a Punic engineer, and a deal with the city.

choices.label: Open the mine
choices.resultText: Silver, some. Slaves, many. The hill is not the hill your children played on. Your ledger is not the ledger you had.

choices.label: Sell the rights to a House with more stomach
choices.resultText: House Iason opens it. Iason gets richer. The hill gets uglier. You get the silver and the sleep.

scene: The old Kleitos groves, the first olives planted outside the wall by Agathon himself, are for sale after a bad succession. They are more famous than they are profitable.

choices.label: Buy them
choices.resultText: Trees older than the wooden wall, yours. Olives obey this hand now, and the city knows whose hand.

choices.label: Pass; fame is not oil
choices.resultText: A Kleitos cousin keeps them. They are still famous. You are still solvent.

scene: An old Ligurian woman, brought to your estate by your shepherds, says your land was once the dowry of Gyptis herself, and that her people still remember the wedding cup.

choices.label: Honor the claim with a feast for her people at the old stone
choices.resultText: Greek wine in Ligurian cups, at a stone nobody knew was a stone. The tribes remember the cup. Now they remember you.

choices.label: Send her home with a coin and a smile
choices.resultText: She goes. The shepherds are quiet a week. The land is exactly as yours as it was, and no more.

scene: Hail flattens the barley the week before harvest. Your tenants stand in the field not saying anything.

choices.label: Remit the year's rent
choices.resultText: They stay. They replant. They tell every other tenant in the chora what you did, and you never have to advertise for hands again.

choices.label: Collect what you can
choices.resultText: Half the rent in goats and grudges. Two families leave at midwinter. The field is very quiet in spring.

scene: A Ligurian neighbor invites your household to his son's wedding: three days, a whole ox, and songs in a language your steward pretends not to know.

choices.label: Go, with a gift and your family
choices.resultText: Three days. You dance, badly. The bride's mother decides you are a good man and tells the whole hill.

choices.label: Send a gift and your steward
choices.resultText: The gift is admired. The steward dances, well. He is asked back; you are not.

scene: The city's new road to Olbia is surveyed straight through your best lower field. The surveyor is open to suggestion.

choices.label: Suggest a bend, with silver
choices.resultText: The road bends. Your field stays. The bend is known, forever, as your bend.

choices.label: Accept the road and claim the compensation
choices.resultText: A straight road, a fair sum, and a roadside stall your tenants run. The bend that isn't there is also known.

scene: Your estate overseer, a slave who has run the place for twenty years, asks to buy himself. He knows every field. He also knows every book.

choices.label: Free him and hire him back
choices.resultText: He works harder as a freedman than he ever did as a slave, which you had not thought possible. The books stay honest.

choices.label: Refuse; he is worth more than his price
choices.resultText: He stays. The books stay honest. He stops offering suggestions, and the estate is worse for it in ways you cannot count.

scene: Threshing is done and the hands expect a feast. The custom is a lamb, wine, and the master dancing once.

choices.label: Give the feast and dance
choices.resultText: You dance once, badly, and it is the thing the hands remember all winter.

choices.label: Pay a coin each instead
choices.resultText: Efficient. The hands drink it in the village and dance without you.

scene: Rats in the granary. A Greek says cats; a Gaulish hand says a snake, one particular snake, from a shrine in the hills.

choices.label: Fetch the snake
choices.resultText: A hill-snake in the granary, and no rats by the month's end. The hands leave it milk. You leave it alone.

choices.label: Cats
choices.resultText: Cats. Fewer rats. A great many cats.

scene: A suitor for your sister asks for the river field as dowry. It is your best field. He is a Miltiades.

choices.label: Give the field
choices.resultText: The wedding is splendid. The field grows Miltiades barley. Your sister is happy, and visits with the barley.

choices.label: Offer the hill field instead
choices.resultText: He takes the hill field, coolly. The wedding is correct. The barley is yours.

scene: A Gaulish hand shows you a heavy wheeled plow his people use in the deep valley soils. It would cut your clay field in half the time.

choices.label: Build one
choices.resultText: The clay field, plowed in a week. Three neighbors ask to borrow the plow. One asks to borrow the Gaul.

choices.label: Keep the Greek scratch-plow
choices.resultText: It works, as it has always worked, slowly. Hesiod's plow. Hesiod's yields.

scene: The Temple of Artemis leases its sacred land in ten-year lots. A lot beside yours is up, cheap, on condition of an offering each harvest.

choices.label: Take the lease
choices.resultText: Good land, a yearly lamb, and the priestess walking your rows at harvest. Tenants behave better on sacred ground.

choices.label: Pass; gods make bad landlords
choices.resultText: A Timon takes the lease and is insufferable about the lamb. The land yields well. So does his piety, in reputation.

scene: The Saluvii, under the new peace, send cattle to graze on the chora as surety. Some have wandered into your barley.

choices.label: Herd them out and send word politely
choices.resultText: A Saluvian herdsman comes for them, apologizes in bad Greek, and leaves a cheese. The peace holds a little harder.

choices.label: Keep two, as damages
choices.resultText: Two good cattle. A chief who counts cattle. A peace that is now your problem too.

scene: Your father's steward dies in the olive rows, as he said he would. His family asks that he be buried on the estate, among the trees he planted.

choices.label: Bury him in the grove
choices.resultText: A stone under the oldest tree. The hands work past it every day and nobody steals so much as an olive from that row.

choices.label: Send him to the village burial ground
choices.resultText: Correct. His sons stay on for wages, and count the years.

scene: Your estate is famous now, and fame draws lawyers. A rival House produces an old deed claiming the river field, and two of the magistrates are its cousins.

choices.label: Settle before the hearing
choices.resultText: The deed disappears into a chest for a price. You keep the field and lose a season's oil.

choices.label: Fight it in open court
choices.resultText: You keep the field. The cousins on the bench say things about your House that are recorded, and read for years.

scene: A laborer dies of a fall in the sacred grove on your land, and the priests declare the whole grove polluted, and you responsible for the purification.

choices.label: Pay for the full rite
choices.resultText: Nine days of salt and hymns at your expense. The grove is clean. The priests' opinion of your stewardship is not.

choices.label: Delay until after harvest
choices.resultText: The harvest comes in. The grove stays polluted a season, and every hand who works past it makes the sign against you.
